why: The student wrote correct, complete code for the familiar minimum task: it starts from data[0], makes one pass keeping the smaller value with Math.min, and prints the result after the loop. That is the running-extreme plan adapted to the minimum, which the boundary for reproducing a familiar program puts at L3, not L4.

concepts.quote: double min = data[0]; for (double v : data) min = Math.min(min, v);
concepts.why: The code builds a working most-wanted holder for the minimum in one pass, and starting at data[0] avoids the start-value pitfall. It is a familiar variant, so L3, not L4.
println is used correctly once, after the loop, to print the final minimum on its own line.
The double variable is declared and assigned correctly from the double array, and its type matches the elements.
The answer makes no claim about integer overflow.
